_note: v2 hook overrides for la Pharmacie (B18_pharmacie). Source hooks are kept where the painting shows them; these replace hooks whose painted scene differs. Medical content is kept gentle: no blood; the needle words are a knitting needle and a blank plaque.

fr_drogue_noun.hook: Said DROG: a blank brass plaque hangs by the locked cabinet for DROGUE, a harmful DRUG that is kept far away. (Medicine you take is le médicament.)
fr_drogue_noun.why: Harmful-substance word, so it is shown only as a blank plaque with no writing.

fr_pharmacie_noun.hook: Sounds like 'fahr-mah-SEE', FAR + SEE: a sea captain peers FAR through his brass telescope to SEE the PHARMACY, and its green cross is hanging right behind him.
fr_pharmacie_noun.why: A sea captain holds the telescope in the painting, not a grandma.

fr_pilule_noun.hook: Sounds like 'pih-LEWL', LULL: a soft round cushion LULLS a hamster to sleep, curled up as small as a PILL.
fr_pilule_noun.why: The cushion is painted round, not pill-shaped.

fr_pharmacien_noun.hook: Sounds like 'fahr-mah-SYAN', FARMER: the bearded PHARMACIST in his white coat hurries past a FARMER and his sneezing cow with a tray for the bear.
fr_pharmacien_noun.why: He carries a tray rather than handing out cough drops, and stands on the right of the shop.

fr_traitement_noun.hook: Sounds like 'treht-MAHN', TRAY + MAN: the pharmacist-MAN brings a TRAY of warm towels and a hot drink: a cosy TREATMENT for the sneezing bear.
fr_traitement_noun.why: The box marks the bear receiving the treatment, so it stays separate from le pharmacien.

fr_sirop_noun.hook: Sounds like 'see-ROH' (silent p), a ROW: the apprentice pours pink cough SYRUP into a bowl for two sniffly kittens sitting in a ROW.
fr_sirop_noun.why: The painting shows two kittens, not three ducklings (the ducklings are in the toy display case).

fr_flacon_noun.hook: Sounds like 'flah-KOHN', almost FLASK: a curious mouse peeks into a tiny glass FLASK, a VIAL of golden medicine on the counter.
fr_flacon_noun.why: No paper funnel is painted; the mouse and its vial carry the hook.

fr_remede_noun.hook: Sounds like 'ruh-MEHD', home-MADE: a beekeeper brings his home-MADE REMEDY, a steaming mug of honey and lemon.
fr_remede_noun.why: Painted as a beekeeper (honey), not a grandma, so it does not repeat the knitting granny.

fr_platre_noun.hook: Sounds like 'PLAHTR', PLATTER: a golden puppy proudly shows off his PLASTER cast covered in paw prints, right beside a shiny silver PLATTER on the floor.
fr_platre_noun.why: The platter is on the floor, not a worktable.

fr_medicament_noun.hook: Sounds like 'may-dee-kah-MAHN', MEDIC + CAR + MAN: a tiny MAN drives a red toy CAR carrying a box of MEDICATION across the floor to a waiting hedgehog.
fr_medicament_noun.why: Matches the painting; the floor, not the counter.

fr_vitamine_noun.hook: Sounds like 'vee-tah-MEEN', MEAN: a tiny ant pushes a glossy orange VITAMIN as big as itself, looking MEAN and mighty.
fr_vitamine_noun.why: The ant pushes the ball along the bottom of the display case rather than lifting it.

fr_cohorte_noun.hook: Sounds like 'koh-ORT', COHORT: a COHORT of five wooden toy ducklings, all made in the same batch, lines up along the bottom of the display case.
fr_cohorte_noun.why: In the display case, not on a display step.

fr_ponction_noun.hook: Said pohnk-SYOHN, close to PUNCTURE: a small blank brass plaque on the display case stands for PONCTION, a medical puncture (and also a deduction of money).
fr_ponction_noun.why: A needle word, so it is kept gentle: a blank plaque only, no needle painted.

fr_filon_noun.hook: Sounds like 'fee-LOHN', FEEL ON: a tiny toy miner FEELS ON along a grey rock and finds a glittering gold VEIN (a LODE).
fr_filon_noun.why: Matches the painting: the miner stands beside the rock.

fr_antibiotique_noun.hook: Sounds like 'ahn-tee-byoh-TEEK', ANTI-: a little toy knight, ANTI-germ, chases two cheerful green germs out of the display case: that is what an ANTIBIOTIC does.
fr_antibiotique_noun.why: Painted as a knight with a star shield, not a capsule.
